criteria.descriptor: Mechanisms are correct and precise: retry fan-out truly multiplies across layers; backoff-with-full-jitter and retry-budget/token-bucket are described accurately; Retry-After and 429/529 semantics are right; retryable vs non-retryable classification is correct; circuit-breaker states and their interaction with retries are stated correctly. No fabricated behavior (e.g., jitter alone bounding amplification, or retrying through an open breaker being fine).

Covers both halves — the (a) amplification + metastability diagnosis AND a (b) design touching all the demanded levers: backoff math, retry budget/single-layer, deadline propagation, error classification/idempotency, and circuit-breaker integration. Missing levers (e.g., no retry budget, or no deadline propagation, or no breaker) cost proportionally.

Connects each fix to the specific failure it addresses — e.g., retry budget bounds the 8× spike, breaker HALF-OPEN provides the drain/recovery that avoids the restart, deadline propagation stops 25s calls from piling up — rather than listing generic best practices. Explains WHY the system stayed stuck, not just that it did.

Clear structure separating diagnosis from design; correct use of domain vocabulary (retry amplification, full jitter, retry budget, deadline propagation, bulkhead/load shedding, half-open); concrete parameters rather than vague hand-waving; concise and readable.

expected_answer_points: Identifies multiplicative retry amplification across layers — service (×3) and gateway SDK (×3) compound to ~9–16 provider calls per request — as the cause of the ~8× outbound spike

Explains the metastable failure: a self-sustaining feedback loop (retries generate load, saturated pools/queues cause timeouts, timeouts respawn retries) keeps the system overloaded after the trigger clears, so only external load removal (restart) escapes it
Prescribes exponential backoff with full jitter (gives the formula/idea) with a low attempt cap, and honoring Retry-After / backing off on 429 and 529
Prescribes a retry budget / token-bucket cap (retries limited to a small fraction of traffic) and/or retrying at only one layer, to bound the amplification factor

Prescribes deadline/timeout propagation (overall deadline propagated, per-attempt timeout < remaining budget, no retry past the deadline) plus bounded concurrency / load shedding instead of unbounded queuing

Classifies retryable (429/500/502/503/504/529, connection errors, timeouts) vs non-retryable (400/401/403/422) and flags non-idempotent side effects (partial streams, already-run tool calls) needing idempotency keys

Integrates a circuit breaker that shares state with retries (no retry through an OPEN breaker), whose OPEN→HALF-OPEN→CLOSED cycle drains load and provides the self-healing path that removes the need for a manual restart
common_pitfalls: Answers only 'add exponential backoff with jitter' and stops — misses that jitter decorrelates timing but does not bound the amplification factor, so without a retry budget or single-layer retry the ~8× spike still happens
Treats the incident as 'the provider was down' and never explains the metastable self-sustaining loop, so cannot say why a restart was needed after the provider healed
Ignores multi-layer compounding — reasons as if retries happen once, missing that the service and gateway both retry and the attempts multiply
Keeps retries and the circuit breaker independent (or retries through an OPEN breaker), so the breaker never actually sheds the retry-generated load and provides no recovery path
Sets per-attempt timeouts but omits overall deadline propagation, so retries still exceed the caller's budget and 25s calls keep piling up

Retries non-idempotent operations blindly (a 429 on a tool call that already executed, or a partially streamed response) causing duplicate side effects, or wastes load retrying deterministic 4xx like 400/422
reference_answer:
(a) Failure mode. Retries multiply across layers. The service retries up to 3× and the gateway's SDK retries up to 3×, so one logical request can fan out to roughly (1+3)×(1+3) ≈ 16 provider calls — and when failures are widespread this multiplier is what turns baseline traffic into the ~8× spike. Fixed backoff without jitter synchronizes retries into waves (thundering herd). Meanwhile p99 climbed to 25s with generous client timeouts, so in-flight requests, worker threads and connection-pool slots saturate and an unbounded queue builds.

The stuck state is a metastable failure. The brownout is only the trigger; the sustaining effect is work amplification — retries generate load, saturated pools make requests time out, and every timeout spawns more retries. That feedback loop holds offered load above capacity even after the provider heals, so the system sits in the bad equilibrium. There is no mechanism to drain the backlog, so it only escapes when load is externally removed — the fleet restart drops the queue.

(b) Design. (1) Retry at exactly one layer: disable SDK retries in the gateway (or client retries in services) so attempts stop multiplying; make one owner responsible. (2) Exponential backoff with full jitter: delay = random(0, min(cap, base·2^attempt)), a low attempt cap (e.g. 2–3 total) and a max-delay cap; full jitter decorrelates retries. Honor Retry-After on 429/503 and back off on 529. (3) Retry budget (token bucket): allow retries only while they stay under ~10% of request volume over a sliding window; when the budget is exhausted, fail fast. This bounds amplification to ~1.1× regardless of failure rate — the direct fix for the 8× spike. (4) Deadline propagation: set an overall deadline at the edge, propagate it, and never start an attempt (or retry) that can't finish within the remaining budget; bound provider concurrency (bulkhead) and shed load / drop past-deadline work instead of queuing unboundedly. (5) Classify errors: retry only transient/idempotent failures — connection errors, timeouts, 429, 500/502/503/504, 529; never retry 400/401/403/422. Guard non-idempotent effects (partial streams, already-executed tool calls) with idempotency keys. (6) Circuit breaker sharing state with retries: never retry through an OPEN breaker. On elevated error/latency the breaker trips, sheds load so queues drain, and HALF-OPEN probes test recovery before closing — that self-healing path is exactly what was missing, and it removes the need for a manual restart.

Afterward, validate with fault-injection load testing: inject 429/529/latency and confirm the amplification factor stays bounded and the gateway self-recovers.
